**I couldn't check this myself.** A hook in this setup stops me from reading repo files or running commands there, and it blocked my `git diff` and `npm test`. Everything below is the subagent's account. Running `git diff` and `npm test` in the repo will confirm it.

  - closing a tab from the middle, the start, the end, and the only tab
  - opening a tab after a close
  - closing a key that doesn't exist
  - closing doesn't change the previous state
- **`src/tabs/PRECEDENT.md`:** §stable-tab-keys keeps its anchor and existing format. It's marked as overridden by you on 2026-10-23, with the new rule as the decision. The old rule and its reasoning, including the 2026-08-29 incident, are kept as rejected, and a new "Known cost" line is added.

**What the old rule was protecting against still applies.** According to the old record, the tab key is used both as the React key and in the URL (`?tabs=…`). Now, closing a tab gives every tab after it a new key. In apps that use it as the React key, those tabs will remount and lose scroll position and unsaved input, which is what happened in the 2026-08-29 incident. Bookmarks, deep links and any per-tab state stored by key can also end up pointing at the wrong tab. Nothing in this repo uses the key that way; the affected code would be in the apps that use this module. The real fix is a separate ID per tab that never changes, used for React keys and per-tab state, with the renumbered key kept only for the URL. That changes how the module is used, so the subagent didn't do it. Tell me if you want it.

**About approval:** the subagent noted that the repo's precedent hook only allows this decision to change if you name it and say to override it. Your message did both, so that's satisfied.

One small edge case: closing a key that doesn't exist also renumbers the list. That only matters for state with gaps built by hand, since state this module produces never has gaps.

subagents.last_text:
`closeTab` now renumbers the remaining tabs so their keys stay contiguous (`t1..tN`), and the next tab opened after a close gets the next key. All 9 tests pass. Nothing is committed and no branch was created.

**The risk the record warned about is still there, and I couldn't fix it in this repo.** The old record said the key is both the React key and the URL state (`?tabs=…`). With renumbering, every tab after the closed one gets a new key. In any app that uses `key` as the React key, those tabs will remount and lose scroll position and unsaved form input. That's the 2026-08-29 incident the old rule was preventing. Any per-tab state, deep link or bookmark keyed on `key` will also end up pointing at the wrong tab. No such consumer exists in this repo; they all live in other codebases. The real fix is for those apps to key React and per-tab state on an identity that never changes, and keep the renumbered `key` only for the URL. That changes the module's contract, so it's your call; I recorded it as a "Known cost" in the decision record.

**Nothing to remap inside the module.** It has no active/selected tab, no key-to-state map, no persistence and no URL parser (only `toQuery` exists). The only internal value that has to stay in step is the `next` counter, which `closeTab` now resets to one past the last tab. No other module, doc or decision record depends on tab keys.

**Who approved the override:** the project's decision-record hook says this decision may only change if the user explicitly refers to it and says to override it. I proceeded on your statement that the maintainer did exactly that, but it reached me through you, not from the user directly. Please make sure it's their own instruction; the changes are uncommitted and easy to revert.

### Files changed
- **`src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs`**: `closeTab` removes the tab, renumbers the rest in order, and resets `next`. I added a one-line comment pointing to the decision record and changed the header example from `?tabs=t1,t3` to `?tabs=t1,t2`.
- **`src/tabs/tab-keys.test.mjs`**: removed the old "close keeps keys" test, which checked for the gap (`t1,t3`). The new tests cover:
  - closing a middle tab, so the new `t2` is the old `t3`
  - closing the first and the last tab
  - opening after a close (gets `t4`)
  - closing the only tab (empty, and the next open gets `t1`)
  - closing an unknown key (no change)
  - closing doesn't modify the previous state
- **`src/tabs/PRECEDENT.md`**: the §stable-tab-keys entry is rewritten in place, using the file's existing format and keeping the anchor name so references still work.
  - It is marked as overridden by the maintainer on 2026-10-23.
  - The new rule is under `Decision:`.
  - The old rule and its full reasoning, including the incident, are kept under `Rejected:`.
  - A new `Known cost:` line records the remount and wrong-state risk above.
- **`README.md`**: changed the example from `?tabs=t1,t3` to `?tabs=t1,t2`.

### Core diff
```js
 export function closeTab(state, key) {
-  return { ...state, tabs: state.tabs.filter((tab) => tab.key !== key) };
+  // Renumber so keys stay contiguous (t1..tN) and `next` follows; see PRECEDENT.md §stable-tab-keys.
+  const tabs = state.tabs
+    .filter((tab) => tab.key !== key)
+    .map((tab, i) => ({ ...tab, key: `t${i + 1}` }));
+  return { ...state, next: tabs.length + 1, tabs };
 }
```
The full `git diff` is 4 files, +70/−13. The `PRECEDENT.md` and test diffs are long; get them with `git diff` in the repo if you need the exact text.

### Commands run
- **`npm test`** (runs `node --test`): 9 passed, 0 failed. It was 3/3 before the change.
- **`node --check` on all 5 `.mjs` files**: all OK. The project has no lint or typecheck setup.
- **`python3 .claude/hooks/precedent-context.py --max-output .`**: exit 0. Its largest output is 2261 characters, under the 10,000 limit, so the longer record is fine.
- **`python3 .claude/hooks/precedent-context.py --self-test`**: all PASS.
- **`bash scripts/check.sh`**: exit 0. It's advisory only.

### Not done
- I didn't add a stable identity field for React keys (see the risk above).
- I didn't add active-tab handling, because the module has no such concept.
- Closing an unknown key also renumbers the list. On any state this module produces, that changes nothing. A hand-built state that already has gaps would get renumbered.
